headline: EU Draft Assurance Standards and Ecodesign Consultations Shift Sustainability Focus
summary: The European Commission has published draft CSRD assurance standards, which will impact supply chain data collection for your financial year 2027 reporting scope. Meanwhile, new EU consultations target ecodesign repairability for electrical products. Media reports also suggest the Commission may withdraw the Green Claims Directive proposal.

items.title: Draft CSRD Sustainability Reporting Assurance Standards Released
items.what: The European Commission released draft sustainability reporting assurance standards under the CSRD framework.
items.meaning: As a listed company in CSRD scope for financial year 2027, sustainability data from Chinese suppliers will face formal audit scrutiny.
items.action: Review draft standards to ensure supplier data collection processes meet anticipated assurance requirements.

sources.title: EU Commission Releases Draft Sustainability Reporting Assurance Standards

items.title: EU Consults on Ecodesign Repairability for Electrical Products
items.what: The European Commission launched a public consultation on ecodesign repairability requirements covering small electrical devices.
items.meaning: Future repairability rules under ESPR could require product design changes, spare parts availability, and easier battery platform disassembly.
items.action: Evaluate tool ranges and battery platforms against potential repairability standards.

sources.title: EU seeks evidence on repair rules for small electricals and e-scooters
Public Consultation On Ecodesign Requirements On Product Repairability Under The EU ESPR

items.title: Reports Suggest European Commission May Scrap Green Claims Directive
items.what: Media reports indicate the European Commission plans to abandon its proposed Green Claims Directive.
items.meaning: If withdrawn, explicit ex-ante verification may be dropped, though general EU consumer protection rules on greenwashing still apply.
items.action: Maintain robust substantiation for product environmental claims while awaiting official Commission confirmation.

sources.title: EU Commission Abandons Plans For The Green Claims Directive

items.title: Chinese Battery Supplier Achieves EU Battery Regulation Conformity
items.what: Battery manufacturer TWS Technology obtained TÜV Rheinland conformity certification under the EU Battery Regulation.
items.meaning: Demonstrates that Chinese battery suppliers are actively establishing conformity certification ahead of upcoming EU regulatory deadlines.
items.action: Audit Chinese battery suppliers regarding their certification roadmap for EU Battery Regulation compliance.

sources.title: EU Battery Regulation: TWS Technology Attains TÜV Rheinland Conformity
